description.narrative:
Background and Justification Uganda has experienced multiple Ebola outbreaks, with the most recent posing a significant threat to both host and refugee communities in the refugee settlements. The South western region hostsa refugee population of 819,799 , (45.3%of the total refugee population in Uganda) primarily from South Sudan (54.2%0 and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC),(31.3%) making disease containment efforts particularly complex. Overcrowded settlements, inadequate water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services, limited access to healthcare, and frequent cross-border movements exacerbate the risk of rapid disease transmission. The refugee settlements face heightened vulnerabilities due to the continued influx of refugees and delays in diagnosis and treatment due tostrained health systems and insufficient preparedness capacities. Given this context, a coordinated and multi-sectoral approach is essential to prevent, detect, and respond to Ebola outbreaks effectively. Oxfam in Uganda, with its extensive experience in humanitarian response <(>&<)> presence in the region, particularly in Water Supply, hygiene/public health promotion and Sanitation (WASH); gender <(>&<)> protection; and community engagement, is well-positioned to contribute significantly to Ebola preparedness and response efforts. Oxfam’s intervention will complement existing initiatives by leveraging its expertise in risk communication and communityengagement (RCCE), safe water supply, and infection prevention and control (IPC) in refugee settlements and host communities. Oxfamin Uganda’s intervention will provide a critical layer of community-based support to ongoing Ebola response efforts the refugees settlements. By focusing on WASH, RCCE, and IPC in refugee settlements, Oxfam will enhance the effectiveness of national and partner-led initiatives. Through coordination with key stakeholders, will ensure a holistic, efficient, and impactful response that minimizesthe spread of Ebola and protects vulnerable refugee populations. Project Goal The overall goal of the project is to reduce the spread of Ebola and other infectious diseases through the provision of essential WASH and IPC support, improving access to clean water, sanitation, and hygiene facilities at both community and healthcare facility levels. This will enhance infection prevention and control measures, contributing to safer healthcare environments, reducing the transmission of Ebola, and supporting affected populationsin quarantine and treatment facilities.
Project Objectives The objectives of this project are as follows: 1.To Improve Access to Safe Water and Sanitation Facilities 2.To Enhance Infection Prevention and Control Measures 3.To Support Vulnerable Populations with Hygiene Kits and Dignity Kits
Key Activities WASH and IPC Support Oxfam in Uganda WASH and IPC support aims to significantly improve the safety and health of communities and healthcare facilities (HCF) by ensuring access to clean water, proper sanitation, and effective infection prevention measures. The proposed activities include: • Borehole Drilling and Installation: We plan to drill high-yielding boreholes at healthcare facilities (HCF) with a future focus on upgrading to a solar-powered system for sustainability and uninterrupted water supply. • Rainwater Harvesting Systems: The installation of stainless-steel-steel rainwater harvesting tanks willbe implemented in schools and healthcare facilities that have intermittent water supply, ensuring access to water in areas prone towater scarcity. • Repair and Rehabilitation of Handpumps: We will restore and enhance existing community water sources by repairinghandpumps, ensuring continued access to safe drinking water. • Gender-sensitive Sanitation Facilities: We will construct institutional drainable latrines at healthcare facilities and schools, designed to be gender-sensitive to ensure dignity and privacy for all users. • Incinerator Construction: Incinerators will be built in healthcare facilities to properly dispose of medical waste, reducingcontamination and promoting environmental safety. • Sanitary Facility Rehabilitation: Existing sanitation facilities at Ebola Treatment Units (ETUs) will be repaired, including desludging filled-up latrines, ensuring safe and hygienic conditions for patients and healthcare workers. • These interventions will be designed to address the immediate needs for clean water and sanitation, ultimatelyenhancing the capacity of healthcare facilities and communities to manage Ebola effectively and reduce the spread of infections. 2.Hygiene Kit Distribution To support vulnerable populations, particularly women, girls, and boys in quarantine centers, we will procure and distribute hygiene kits containing essential items. These kits will include: • Basic Hygiene Items: Buckets, bar soap, toothpaste, undergarments, sanitary supplies, razors, disinfectants, and more. • Non-contact Handwashing Facilities: Installation of handwashing stations in healthcare facilities and public areas, such as schools and markets, to encourage frequent hand hygiene. • WasteManagement: Procurement and distribution of 20 waste collection bins for healthcare facilities to manage waste efficiently and reduce contamination risks. • Dignity Kits: Distribution of dignity kits specifically for women and adolescent girls in ETUs to ensure their comfort and hygiene during treatment and quarantine. These efforts will ensure that essential hygiene supplies reach the most vulnerable, reinforcing their ability to protect themselves from infection during the Ebola response. 3. IPC Material Development andHealth Worker Training A critical component of this intervention is the development of IPC materials and the training of healthcareworkers. Oxfam will: • IPC Materials: Print and distribute Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) awareness materials, including posters, brochures, leaflets, and stickers, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health (MoH). These materials will be available in local languages for better understanding and engagement. • Health Worker Training: In partnership with the MoH, we will conduct comprehensive IPC training for healthcare workers (HCWs) and community health volunteers (CHVs). The training will cover IPC assessments,monitoring of healthcare facilities, and the use of tools such as WASHFIT, checklists, and audit tools to ensure proper infection control protocols are followed. The monitoring process for the relief operation. The monitoring and learning systems will include structured data collection, real-time analysis, and feedback loops to ensure informed decision-making. Progress will be tracked and assessed before, during, and after project execution with technical assistance from technical leads. With assistance from the technicalleads, Programme quality and learning lead, and MEAL personnel, the project will be efficiently monitored in accordance with approved relevant documents including Ebola Response Plan for Mbale and Mbale City, approved response workplan and Logical Framework (LF).Through post-distribution monitoring (PDM), and routine data collection from the field. We will make significant investments in thediligent gathering and analysis of quantitative and qualitative data. Household surveys, FGDs and KIIs will be used for participatory monitoring and evaluation. Data Collection <(>&<)> Disaggregation – Regular surveys, system-generated reports, and stakeholder feedback will be used to gather qualitative and quantitative data, disaggregated by key demographic and contextual factors (e.g., gender, age, location). Monitoring Framework – A robust monitoring framework will track progress against key performance indicators (KPIs), using tools such as dashboards, data management systems, and periodic reviews. Data Analysis <(>&<)> Review – Collected data will be analyzed to identify trends, disparities, and areas for improvement. Regular review meetings will be held monthly by the MEAL team to interpret the findings and ensure alignment with project goals. Adaptive Learning <(>&<)> Decision-Making – Insights from data analysis will be integrated into decision-making processes, allowing for agile responses, course corrections, and continuous improvement based on real-time evidence. Stakeholder Engagement – Findings will be shared with key stakeholders, including project teams,partners, and beneficiaries, to enhance transparency, accountability, and collaborative problem-solving.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
